goal: Use one latest-only profiler format for offline storage and TCP transport, remove conflicting legacy profiler paths without compatibility, and organize the migration through milestone-owned stage checkpoint files under docs/milestones grouped by requirement domain.

implementation_status.current_stage: M1 mostly landed, preparing broader deletion follow-through
recently_completed: ProfileDump schema metadata now carries event_type and the parser/tests dispatch through event_type instead of schema name.
Built-in timing templates were extracted from ProfileDump.h into profile/ProfileDumpTemplates.h so producer and consumer code can share canonical declarations.
MoerProfiler now ingests canonical ProfileDump packets over TCP and from offline binary files instead of using the old Trace TCP plus CSV-only consumer boundary.
MoerProfiler consumer storage now uses local profiler-owned event/session/track types instead of depending on trace/Trace.h as its in-memory model.
The profiler consumer implementation is now centralized in source/profiler/ProfileSession.h/.cpp and enforces session-relative normalized timestamps in one place.
Focused profiler-side normalization coverage now exists in testscripts/windows/test_rhi_translate.ps1 through the TestRHITranslate target.
next_execution_focus: Delete the remaining repository-wide legacy profiler surfaces, especially the public source/profile role and Trace transport APIs that still survive outside the profiler app consumer path.
Extend canonical event_type dispatch beyond CPU/GPU scope events once the normalized store contract is frozen.
Decide whether session metadata must be emitted as an explicit canonical ProfileDump record rather than being inferred from first-event origin in the consumer.

document_contract.grouping_rule: Milestone files must live under a requirement-specific subfolder such as profiler, renderer, editor, or runtime. Do not flatten unrelated milestone families directly under docs/milestones.
document_contract.update_rule: Any temporary requirement change or replan must update both the owning milestone file and the affected stage checkpoint file instead of changing only one side.
document_contract.checkpoint_rule: Each stage owns its own checkpoint file. Checkpoint content must follow the existing repository checkpoint style: explicit problem statement, execution order, what must be true after each checkpoint, likely affected files, risks, and validation through existing scripts only.

streaming_capable.notes: Current live MoerProfiler ingest format. It is transport-specific, too narrow, and forces a second profiler schema model beside ProfileDump.
Current structured binary schema+record stream. It already has the right hot-path, sink, and parser shape for the long-term canonical contract.

offline_or_legacy.notes: Offline only. Not suitable as canonical profiler storage because it is text-heavy, schema-poor, and duplicates parsing/export logic.
The source/profile module still exists as a separate public profiler surface. That conflicts with the unified MoerProfiler direction and should not survive as a peer stack.

format_decision.best_offline_format: ProfileDump append-only binary file backed by the same packet contract used on the wire
why_profile_dump_wins_offline: It is already structured, versioned, and schema-driven.
It avoids CSV text overhead and ad-hoc column evolution.
It matches the parser/test direction already landed in current focused tests.
why_profile_dump_wins_for_tcp: It already separates schema packets and record packets so the consumer can evolve without hard-coded packet families.
It avoids JSON or CSV serialization cost on the producer hot path.
It lets file and network share one semantic contract instead of keeping Trace-specific transport beside a different offline format.

rejected_as_canonical.name: Trace custom metadata/events packet format
rejected_as_canonical.reason: It preserves a second transport contract and a second profiler schema model.

rejected_as_canonical.name: Trace CSV
rejected_as_canonical.reason: It is not a serious canonical profiler format.

rejected_as_canonical.name: Chrome Trace JSON
rejected_as_canonical.reason: It can exist later as a downstream exporter, but not as the canonical storage or transport layer.

rejected_as_canonical.name: Keep source/profile as a parallel public profiler subsystem
rejected_as_canonical.reason: That keeps legacy duplication alive and contradicts the latest-only migration rule.

public_paths_to_remove: Trace packet serialization/deserialization as the profiler transport contract
Trace CSV export as a canonical offline path
source/profile public role as a separate profiler system
Any code path that makes MoerProfiler ingest Trace packets directly instead of ProfileDump packets
delete_without_compatibility.migration_rule: No fallback path survives once the canonical ProfileDump path lands. Any remaining helper macro or producer utility must emit canonical ProfileDump records directly and must not hide the old contract behind a wrapper.

hard_constraints.title: One profiler format only
hard_constraints.detail: After migration, there is exactly one canonical profiler transport and storage contract: ProfileDump packets.

hard_constraints.title: No compatibility shims
hard_constraints.detail: Do not keep Trace packet transport, CSV ingestion, or source/profile as fallback compatibility once equivalent ProfileDump behavior exists.

hard_constraints.title: One normalized time model
hard_constraints.detail: Profiler storage, file output, TCP transport, and UI rendering must use one session-relative time model instead of leaking raw clock-domain values.

hard_constraints.title: One consumer model
hard_constraints.detail: MoerProfiler must parse one canonical packet family and build one canonical event/session store from it.

hard_constraints.title: Existing repository scripts only
hard_constraints.detail: Implementation validation must stay on current repository scripts such as testscripts/windows/test_rhi_translate.ps1 and testscripts/windows/test_all.ps1.

stages.title: Freeze canonical format and delete conflicting public paths
stages.why: Current profiler work is blocked by parallel contracts: Trace packets, CSV, ProfileDump, and the legacy source/profile module. This stage removes the ambiguity before more features land.
exit_criteria: There is one written decision that ProfileDump is the only canonical file and TCP format.
The session-relative time contract is frozen.
The delete list for Trace CSV, Trace packet transport, and legacy source/profile is explicit and non-optional.

stages.title: Rewrite runtime producers onto one ProfileDump contract
stages.why: Runtime emission must stop publishing Trace-specific transport packets and instead publish canonical ProfileDump records for CPU, GPU, counters, instants, and metadata.
exit_criteria: CPU and GPU producers emit canonical ProfileDump records directly.
Trace packet transport APIs are removed or reduced to local migration helpers with no public transport role.
File and TCP output share the same canonical packet writer.

stages.title: Rewrite MoerProfiler ingest, storage, and offline loading
stages.why: MoerProfiler must stop being a Trace-packet plus CSV application and become a ProfileDump consumer with one canonical storage and indexing path.
exit_criteria: MoerProfiler loads canonical binary files and canonical TCP packets through one parser path.
The UI uses one normalized session model and no longer imports CSV.
Timeline correctness no longer depends on raw absolute timestamps leaking through the UI.

stages.title: Add richer semantics and scale-oriented storage
stages.why: Once the format and consumer model are stable, richer profile kinds and heavy-data optimizations can land without re-breaking ownership.
exit_criteria: Counter, instant, async, memory, and other profile kinds use the same canonical contract.
Large sessions remain interactable through indexed and cached storage.
Any optional external exporter is downstream of the canonical store rather than a parallel ingestion path.

validation: Current implementation already builds with cmake --build build --config Debug and produces MoerProfiler.exe with the canonical ProfileDump consumer path compiled in.
Focused validation now includes profiler-side normalization and stream consumer coverage through testscripts/windows/test_rhi_translate.ps1.
Broader repository validation passed through testscripts/windows/test_all.ps1 after the shared consumer module and normalization landing.
When implementation starts, update both the milestone file and the affected stage checkpoint file together.
Do not add a new standalone primary profiler script for this migration.
